verdict.rationale: Bento lets users write alert rules in plain English. These rules compile to trace queries, fire in real time on matching events, and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook. It also mentions trigger-based fixes (skills, subagents, tools) that roll out automatically after shadow-mode scoring. However, the documented actions are mostly notification and routing, and all evidence comes from marketing and FAQ claims rather than detailed rule-configuration docs. Missing for 10: documented rule/action configuration syntax, arbitrary custom actions beyond alert routing, webhook payload details, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Alerts are defined in plain natural language... Rules compile to trace queries and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook.
Bento trains a detector on your own traces, fires it in real time, and backfills your history.
Reusable, trigger-based fixes: skills, subagents, and tools that graduate from candidate to promote as they prove themselves in production.
